decisive_items: Immunostaining: Positive for CD34, CD10, CD19; negative for CD20 and CD33
response.rationale: B-lymphoid blast immunophenotype (CD10/CD19+, CD20-, CD33-) with 60% marrow blasts and Philadelphia chromosome establishes acute lymphoblastic leukemia; R6 is too nonspecific, and other candidates explain only background conditions or lack hematologic evidence.

rejected.why: Hypertension alone cannot explain marrow blasts and B-lymphoid immunophenotype; CT/MRI unremarkable.
Diabetes is background; does not account for blasts or Philadelphia chromosome.
Hyperglycemia may affect cognition but is contradicted by marrow blasts and immunophenotype.
Factor V Leiden is historical thrombophilia, not the cause of acute leukemia.
Factor V Leiden thrombophilia does not explain marrow blasts.
Diabetes mellitus is background; no link to B-lymphoid blasts.
Patient has hypothyroidism, not hyperthyroidism; Philadelphia-positive ALL is not hyperthyroidism-related.
No leukoencephalopathy on MRI; marrow blasts and immunophenotype are decisive.
Philadelphia/p210 and basophilia suggest CML, but 60% blasts with CD10/CD19-positive, CD33-negative lymphoid blasts favor ALL.
No thrombocytopenia/schistocytes; marrow blasts and immunophenotype indicate leukemia, not TTP.
TSH is normal; hypothyroidism is background and does not explain blasts.
TSH normal and no thyroid-related dementia; marrow findings are diagnostic.
